summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic graft-versus-host disease, prior stem cell transplant, and history of venous thromboembolism was admitted after worsening chest pain following a motor vehicle accident three days prior. Imaging revealed an acute sternal fracture and an acute left 6th rib fracture, with no evidence of intrathoracic injury. She was admitted for pain control and monitoring. Pain was initially managed with oxycodone and a lidocaine patch, then transitioned to hydromorphone (Dilaudid) for better control. She remained hemodynamically stable, afebrile, and was able to ambulate and tolerate oral intake. Incentive spirometry was used to prevent pulmonary complications. She was discharged home with services on hospital day 3 with a pain regimen including acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and PRN hydromorphone, along with continued enoxaparin for thromboprophylaxis. Follow-up was arranged with her primary care provider.
